channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement six waste-to-energy projects by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing six investment projects to improve waste management and generate electricity from waste by 2026-2027. The total cost is $933 million, with $286.8 million invested as of September 1. These projects, in cooperation with Chinese companies, will process 3.6 million tons of waste annually, producing 1.6 billion kWh of electricity.

item.title: Uzbekistan to host first Central Asian Student Sports Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the first Central Asian Student Sports Forum from September 29 to October 2, 2026. The event aims to promote Uzbekistan's experience in student sports development internationally and strengthen cooperation among Central Asian nations. FISU president and representatives from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan are expected to attend.

item.title: Tashkent's modernist architecture inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
item.description: Uzbekistan's national nomination 'Tashkent's Modernist Architecture. Central Asian Modernity and Traditions' has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. This marks Uzbekistan's first national inclusion in the list in 25 years, recognizing 10 iconic modernist sites in Tashkent and opening opportunities for cultural tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Create Digital Platform for Cultural Heritage Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce a new Heritage Impact Assessment system to protect historical cities like Bukhara and Samarkand, and Tashkent's modernist architecture. A unified digital platform for cultural heritage will be created, including digital twins of sites and an open data system. Digitization of all heritage sites is planned by 2030.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Fully Digitize Cultural Heritage Sites by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully digitize its cultural heritage sites by 2030. Proposals include creating a unified digital platform, digital twins of heritage objects, and an open data system. A situational center will monitor sites using IoT sensors, satellite data, and AI. Visitor management systems will also be implemented.

item.title: ADB delegation reviews Uzbekistan's pharmaceutical sector reforms and potential
item.description: A delegation from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) met with officials from Uzbekistan's Agency for the Development of Medical and Pharmaceutical Industry. They discussed reforms, quality improvement measures, and preparations for joining the Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S). The ADB positively assessed reforms and expressed interest in future collaborations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Fines 22 Banks and 3 Microfinance Organizations
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank imposed fines on 22 banks and 3 microfinance organizations in August for violations. These included non-compliance with prudential norms, legal deviations, and issues found during inspections and mystery shopper controls.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Discuss Further Development of Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister Ayşe Berris Ekinci. They welcomed the results of political consultations and noted the dynamic development of their comprehensive strategic partnership. Discussions also covered current international and regional issues and upcoming bilateral events.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy inventories all international grants
item.description: The Ministry of Economy of Kyrgyzstan is conducting an inventory of all active and completed international grant and technical assistance projects. The ministry aims to improve the efficiency of fund utilization. Deputy Minister Mederbek Tumanov stated that a unified database is being formed to assess project results.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry Audits International Grants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy is conducting an inventory of all active and completed international grant and technical assistance projects. The ministry aims to improve the efficiency of fund utilization by creating a unified database and evaluating project outcomes.

item.title: Central Asian Foreign Ministers Advocate for Strengthening Global Nuclear Security
item.description: Foreign ministers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan issued a joint statement on the 20th anniversary of the Central Asian Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone Treaty. They reaffirmed commitment to the treaty's goals, emphasizing its role in regional security and nuclear disarmament, while expressing concern over stalled arms control progress.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Harvests Over 760,000 Tons of Wheat Amid Increased Yields
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has harvested over 760,000 tons of wheat, contributing to a total grain harvest of 1.37 million tons, an increase of 189,700 tons from the previous year. The Ministry of Water Resources and Agriculture reported that average yields rose by 2.8 centners per hectare. Harvesting continues across the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Harvests Over 760,000 Tons of Wheat
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has harvested over 760,000 tons of wheat and a total of 1.37 million tons of grain this year, surpassing last year's figures. The Ministry of Agriculture reports higher yields for major crops, with harvesting ongoing and Chuiskaya Oblast leading in grain production.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Produce 1.6 Billion kWh of Electricity Annually from Waste Incineration
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to generate 1.6 billion kWh of electricity annually by incinerating waste. Six investment projects in cooperation with Chinese companies are scheduled for 2026-2027, with a total value of $933 million. This initiative aims to address waste management and energy production.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Participation in International Civil Aviation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has ratified protocols amending the Convention on International Civil Aviation. These amendments aim to broaden member state representation in ICAO's governing bodies and ensure more balanced regional interests in decision-making. The ratified law establishes a legal framework for increased Uzbek participation in the organization's institutional reforms.

item.title: White House Removes Anti-Immigrant Video Game After Tetris Condemnation
item.description: The White House has removed an anti-immigrant video game, 'Build the Wall,' from its website after it faced criticism, including from Tetris. The game, which resembled Tetris, required players to build a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border. Tetris stated its belief in unity, not division.

item.title: Uzbekistan's National Guard Tasked with Suppressing Mass Riots
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved amendments to the National Guard Law, assigning it the new task of suppressing mass riots. This update aims to systematize the Guard's duties, consolidate functions related to public safety and order, and eliminate legislative gaps. The National Guard, established in 2017, has seen its legal status and powers expanded through numerous laws and decrees.

item.title: Asadjon Khojayev Appointed Deputy Minister of Digital Technologies in Uzbekistan
item.description: Asadjon Khojayev has been appointed as the Deputy Minister of Digital Technologies in Uzbekistan. He will serve as the Deputy Minister for Compliance and Internal Control Against Corruption. This appointment is part of the ongoing efforts to strengthen governance in the digital sector.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accelerates Development of Electrical Engineering Industry
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans to boost Uzbekistan's electrical engineering sector and production of competitive goods. The industry's output grew from 4.7 trillion soums in 2018 to 43.1 trillion soums, with exports exceeding $1 billion to 65 countries. Significant investments have created new jobs, and production now includes solar panels, EV charging stations, and high-voltage equipment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Chair: Poverty Reduction Means Improving Lives, Not Just Numbers
item.description: Tanzila Narbaeva, Chair of the Uzbek Senate, emphasized that reducing poverty is about enhancing human dignity and improving lives, not just statistical changes. She highlighted that poverty in Uzbekistan has decreased from 35% to 4% due to a comprehensive approach including financial aid, job creation, and targeted social support. This has led to a significant reduction in the number of low-income citizens.

item.title: NATO Thwarts Russian Secret Arctic Operation Near Svalbard
item.description: NATO forces from the US, UK, and Norway have stopped Russian submarines near the Svalbard archipelago. The submarines were reportedly attempting to test a new weapon designed to disable global internet cables.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Health Center Advises on Simple Prevention Measures for Respiratory Infections
item.description: As autumn arrives, Kyrgyzstan's Republican Health Promotion Center reminds citizens about preventing acute respiratory viral infections (ARVI). Recommendations include frequent hand washing, avoiding contact with sick individuals, not touching the face with dirty hands, practicing cough etiquette, and wearing masks in public when illness levels rise.

item.title: Tashkent Proposes Raising Bus and Metro Fares to 2,500 Som
item.description: A draft document released for public discussion in Tashkent proposes increasing bus and metro fares starting October 1. The proposed fare is 2,500 som for electronic payments and 3,000 som for cash. Discounted tariffs will apply to transport cards.

item.title: Automated Air Quality Monitoring Station Opens in Osh, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: An automated air quality monitoring station has been launched at Osh State University as part of an international project. The station will provide continuous monitoring and collect accurate data on air pollution in Osh. Representatives from the Osh mayor's office, JICA, and the Tokyo Institute of Technology attended the opening ceremony.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Commission for Cultural Property Repatriation
item.description: Uzbekistan will form a commission to systematically search for, legally protect, and return cultural assets taken abroad. The commission, operating under the President, aims to recover stolen heritage.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Utilize Over 46,000 First-Floor Apartments for Business
item.description: Over 46,000 first-floor apartments in Uzbekistan can be used for trade and services without reclassifying them as non-residential property. This initiative is expected to create jobs and boost incomes, according to the Construction Ministry.

item.title: Leaders Not Understanding Current Politics Will Be Dismissed, Says Mirziyoyev
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev warned leaders that poverty reduction efforts must go beyond meetings and reports. He criticized officials sent from Tashkent for staying in offices instead of visiting neighborhoods to understand the real situation and guide local authorities.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves Alphabet Changes, Adopting 28 Latin-Based Letters
item.description: The Uzbek Senate has approved amendments to the law on the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The new alphabet will feature 28 letters and an apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three letter combinations. Documents and currency issued under the old alphabet will remain valid during the transition period.

item.title: Tajikistan authorities recruit citizens for work in Turkey and Russia
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Employment Agency is recruiting citizens for jobs in Turkey and Russia. Positions include skilled labor, drivers, and construction workers. Salaries range from $700-$1250 in Turkey and 80,000-140,000 rubles in Russia.

item.title: Environmental inspector dies in Sirdaryo while stopping illegal fishing
item.description: An environmental inspector in Sirdaryo died while attempting to stop individuals engaged in illegal fishing with electric nets. The inspector fell into the water during the confrontation and his body was recovered the next day. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Tajik teenager faces criminal charges for allegedly stabbing another minor in Badakhshan
item.description: Tajikistan's Interior Ministry reported that a criminal case has been opened against a 15-year-old boy in Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region suspected of stabbing another minor. The incident occurred on September 7 near the "Chorbogh" park in Khorugh, where the suspect allegedly attacked a 14-year-old with a knife.

item.title: Pakistan warns Iran to restrain Houthis, conveys Saudi message
item.description: Pakistan has warned Iran to restrain the Houthi group and conveyed an official message from Saudi Arabia. This measure is being taken to prevent the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Tajik businessman admits sending sanctioned equipment to Russia in US court
item.description: A Tajik businessman has admitted in a US court to sending sanctioned equipment to Russia. The details of the case and the specific equipment involved were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Tajik businessman arrested in US for sanctions violations against Russia has been released
item.description: Salimjon Nasriddinov, a Tajik businessman detained in the US nearly three years ago for allegedly sending sanctioned equipment to Russia, has been released. His family declined to provide further details, and the terms of his release are unknown. Nasriddinov had pleaded guilty to the charges in a New York federal court.

item.title: Expert discusses German election results and the rise of the AfD party
item.description: An expert analyzes the recent German federal state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD party secured a significant victory with 43.8% of the vote. The article discusses potential coalition scenarios and the implications of the AfD's growing influence on Germany's party system, noting the traditional refusal of major parties to cooperate with the far-right.

item.title: Ecological police officer killed in the line of duty confronting illegal fishing
item.description: An ecological police inspector died while on duty after confronting individuals engaged in illegal fishing using electric seines. The incident occurred when the inspector encountered the offenders resisting his attempts to stop their activity. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Announces Further Decrease in Dollar Exchange Rate
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has announced the official exchange rate for foreign currencies against the Uzbek som, effective September 11. The dollar exchange rate has seen a further decrease. The bank regularly publishes these rates, influencing the country's financial market.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree aims to reduce state interference and strengthen protections for businesses, fostering economic growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes six-month licensing for LED lamp imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a six-month mandatory licensing system for importing LED lamps. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce would issue single-use licenses, requiring prior approval from the Ministry of Energy. This aims to curb uncontrolled imports and support domestic producers.

item.title: Foreign national detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was detained at Osh International Airport on suspicion of smuggling Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security reported the operation involved customs officers. A criminal case for economic smuggling has been opened, and the damage to the state budget is being determined.
